messages:
IncidentBot: PAGER: high-sev — GPU OOMs observed on pool=dedicated-gpu-1, 6 container restarts in last 5m. severity=high. affected-models: >16k-context variants. suggested responders: @jamie-oncall @priya-sre @marco-runtime :rotating_light:
Jamie (oncall): seeing the alert, joining. I'm paged. starting triage. :coffee:
Priya (sre): logs look like classic prefill OOMs; GPU memory skyrockets during prefill for long conversations. grabbing kube events now.
Marco (runtime): fyi we've seen similar with large thread+tools combos — prefill tries to allocate full KV cache then hits OOM. adding runtime trace.
Tia (support): any customer impact yet? Support has one ticket from Acme where they saw failed responses.
Jamie (oncall): Acme and BetaHealth reported errors. linking ticket ids: ACME-872, BHE-221. marking customer-impacting.
Priya (sre): kube events: 3 containers OOMKilled, reason: OOMKilled, restartCount: 3. node metrics show GPUs at ~98% before crash. snippet:
```
kubectl -n inference describe pod prefill-worker-57ff
Events:
  Warning  OOMKilled  10s  kubelet  Container prefill exited with status OOMKilled
Last state: Terminated: Exit Code 137
```

Marco (runtime): runtime logs show cuda out of memory during prefill kernel alloc: "RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 5.12 GiB". full snippet:
```
2026-03-15T09:12:03Z runtime ERROR prefill: cuda out of memory while allocating 5505024000 bytes
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/app/serve/prefill.py", line 412, in prefill_step
    kv_cache = torch.empty((batch, seq_len, kv_size), device='cuda')
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 5.12 GiB (GPU 0; 31.75 GiB total, 30.2 GiB already allocated)
```

Priya (sre): immediate mitigation options: 1) cordon/evacuate noisy nodes, 2) apply per-request prefill clamp so worker doesn't pre-allocate max seq_len, 3) route long-context requests to fallback small-context model.
Jamie (oncall): Plan: short-term — apply clamp + route new long-context requests to fallback. Medium — revert prefill behavior with patch to avoid full allocation. Long — QA and rollout kernel-level allocation guard. I'll take short-term.
Marco (runtime): I can push a hotfix: add a prefill allocation cap env var PREFILL_MAX_ALLOC_MB and fall back to streaming prefill. Patch ready, needs quick redeploy. Example change:
```
# runtime config
PREFILL_MAX_ALLOC_MB=4096
# behavior: if predicted alloc > PREFILL_MAX_ALLOC_MB -> stream-prefill mode
```

Priya (sre): while Marco prepares, I'll add taints to the most impacted nodes and drain any obviously noisy pods. issuing command now.
Marco (runtime): redeploying runtime hotfix to pool=dedicated-gpu-1 (canary 10%). Deploy command:
```
kubectl -n inference set env ds/prefill-runtime PREFILL_MAX_ALLOC_MB=4096 --record
kubectl rollout restart ds/prefill-runtime
```

Tia (support): drafting customer update: "We're seeing OOMs affecting long-context requests; engineers identified mitigations and are rolling a hotfix and routing changes. No data loss; transient errors for some requests. ETA 30-45m." ok to send?
Evan (product): yes send that, call out that short-context requests unaffected. keep tone: we have mitigations rolling.
Jamie (oncall): sent to ACME and BetaHealth: "We deployed a mitigation to reduce memory pre-allocation for large-context requests; you may see improved success rates in ~10 min. We'll follow up with root cause." logged.
Priya (sre): initial canary shows fewer restarts on 10% of pods. monitoring.
Marco (runtime): canary logs: prefill allocation now capped, no immediate OOM on canary. pushing to 50% if stable.
Priya (sre): scaling 10->50% now. also enabling eviction policy: prefer-kill=smallest-liveness? (jk) — actually setting podDisruptionBudget low temporarily.
Jamie (oncall): note: we saw a noisy workload from BetaHealth: repeated 60k-token prepends from a debug script. request scope enforcement ticket created.
Tia (support): BetaHealth acknowledged they had a misconfigured test harness hitting prod — they paused tests. good.
Priya (sre): at +22m after mitigation, cluster GPU OOM events dropped from ~6/5m to 0/5m on patched pods. still watching.
Marco (runtime): follow-up tasks: 1) add runtime guard to compute predicted alloc before allocating and fall back to streaming; 2) add telemetry for prefill predicted alloc distribution; 3) add soft quota per-tenant for long-context. I'll open PRs.
Jamie (oncall): creating incident ticket INC-2026-001 for postmortem. assigning owners: Marco -> runtime fixes, Priya -> infra safeguards + node rotation playbook update, Tia -> customer comms and timeline.
Evan (product): add product follow-up: consider prefill-size header and API-level rejection for >X tokens to prevent accidental abuse.
Priya (sre): final status (t+38m): rollout to 100% done, restarts returned to baseline, customer errors reduced to 1 open ticket (ACME) being manually retried. marking incident as mitigated.
Jamie (oncall): handing off to oncall tomorrow: @next-oncall (reminder: follow PRs and ensure postmortem posted). closing pager for now. :white_check_mark:
Marco (runtime): uploading patch links in INC-2026-001 and adding logs for the canary run. PR: https://git.redwood/inference/runtime/pulls/321
Tia (support): sent final customer update: "Mitigation deployed and validated; no data lost. We'll share a postmortem and ETA for permanent fix."
IncidentBot: Incident INC-2026-001 created and assigned. severity downgraded to low (mitigated).
Jamie (oncall): extra notes for postmortem: include timeline, emergency hotfix steps, customer impact table, and recommended API change (prefill-size header). tagging Priya/Marco for drafts.
Marco (runtime): quick snippet to reproduce locally (DO NOT RUN ON PROD):
```
# repro: long-context prefill stress
python -m tools/prefill_stress --model gpt-large-16k --seq 65000 --parallel 8 --repeat 500
```

Jamie (oncall): last check-in: stable for 1h, closing incident channel. thanks team. :pray:
